title: Armstrong leaves Collins and stays with the du Conges
summary: In 1933 Armstrong, who discovered his manager Collins was making vastly more than paid him, left London and stayed with Pete du Conge and Bricktop at Bouchevalles.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well, this was -- let me just get the years straight. This must have been around 1933,

when Duke was in there. Yes, that's just when it was. Yeh, 1933, and around about that time, Louie Armstrong had difficulties with his managing director, Mr. Collins, in London, and left there and there were some difficulties together.
It appeared that Louie found out that Mr. Collins was making some, almost 20,000 pounds a week for him, and Louie was getting about 100 pounds a week.
You see. And he asked for more money, and Mr. Collins, he used some beautiful adjectives, you see.

And Louie, Peter du Congé, he is the one who explained everything, because he was in charge of the orchestra, so we helped finish this contract at the Palladium in London, and came over to Paris, with
And he lived at Peter's home, because they had -- Peter and Bricktop had a beautiful home in -- wait a minute, I lived right across the street -- Bouchevalles.
Oh, it's out in the suburbs?
In the suburbs, yes. On the way to Versailles.
And, Louie lived with them, Louie and his wife. I don't remember her name.-- Lucille, yeh.
His first wife, Lucille. It wasn't the piano player -- what's her name?
His first wife was the piano player that played with Joe Oliver's orchestra.
And then he had a girl friend that he had when he was here. They weren't married. I know her name -- but anyway, it's not Lucille, she came later.
Lucille is later. Well, I know her too, 'cause she lived at Bricktop's.
So Bricktop had what, a big place out at --
She had a big place, yeh. She had a big private home. At Bouchevalles.
